anatomy.name: trigger

anatomy.name: panel

anatomy.description: Arbitrary, potentially interactive content rendered inside the panel.

content.description: Rendered inside the floating panel while open is true.

open.description: Controlled visibility. Popup has no internal open state and no defaultOpen.

onOpenChange.description: Called with false on Escape or an outside click. Popup does not change its own visibility.

alignment.description: Preferred side/edge alignment. Falls back to whichever of the six overflows the viewport least.

closeOnOutsideClick.description: Calls onOpenChange(false) on a pointer press outside the trigger and panel.

id.description: Id applied to the panel and to the trigger's aria-controls while open. Generated via React.useId when omitted.

role.description: ARIA role for the panel. No default - depends on what the consumer is building.

className.description: Composes with the panel's class list.

unstyled.description: Skips Popup's own visual skin (background, border, padding, radius, shadow), leaving only structural positioning and the mount animation. Set this when a consumer has an entirely different visual design of its own - e.g. Tooltip.

padding.description: Padding for Popup's own visual skin, mapped to the spacing scale (none=0, sm=--spacing-sm, md=--spacing-md, lg=--spacing-lg). Lets a consumer size the skin (e.g. a menu's denser rows, or a consumer whose own content manages all edge padding) while still sharing background/border/radius/shadow. Ignored when unstyled is true.

manageTriggerAria.description: Sets aria-expanded/aria-controls on the trigger while true. Set to false when the consumer already manages the trigger's own ARIA relationship to the panel content (e.g. Tooltip's aria-describedby) - aria-expanded/aria-controls are disclosure-widget attributes and don't apply to a supplemental hint.

tokens.note: --color-elevation-shadow-overlay-spread and -perimeter were added alongside this component - they mirror the existing --color-elevation-shadow-raised-* family's shape, using the exact alpha values (16%, 32%) read from Figma's Light/elevation.shadow.overlay effect style. The dark-theme values mirror elevation.shadow.raised's light-to-dark base-hue swap at the same percentages rather than an independently re-verified dark effect.

triggeredBy: consumer-controlled - Popup attaches no open/close handler itself
accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the trigger, reflecting open, unless manageTriggerAria is false
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the trigger to the panel id only while open, unless manageTriggerAria is false; preserves an existing value while closed
accessibility.focusManagement: left to the consumer - Popup does not move focus into or out of the panel
requirements: aria-expanded reflects open on the trigger by default (manageTriggerAria=true).
aria-controls points at the panel id only while open, by default.
manageTriggerAria=false skips both attributes entirely, for consumers with their own trigger ARIA relationship (e.g. aria-describedby).
No default role is added to the panel - the consumer supplies one appropriate to its content.
Popup does not make the trigger focusable or change its semantics beyond the two aria attributes above.

figmaSource.structure: Two component properties beyond the variant axes: an exposed SLOT (the anchor/trigger region) and an internal, unpromoted Slot inside the nested `figma-parts / popup` panel instance (the content region). Code models this as `children` (trigger) + `content` (panel content) rather than two Figma-shaped slot props, since the inner slot was never promoted to the outer component set's own property list.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's `isOpen` variant became the `open` prop, not `isOpen` - `open` is a native HTML attribute (dialog/details), and component-api-governance.json prefers native names whenever one exists.

`alignment`'s default (`topLeft`) matches Figma's own declared default variant exactly, even though a click-opened floating panel more typically opens below its trigger - there was no product signal in the source file to justify overriding it.

Dismissal (Escape/outside click) has no Figma variant at all - it's a code-level behavior decision, not a design-source fact. Added as opt-out (default on) rather than opt-in, so most consumers get it for free.

padding gained a fourth value, `none`, on 2026-08-19 when Dropdown Menu was built on top of Popup: its Figma instance of `popup` wraps a `menu` panel with zero outer padding around it (the menu's own search field and rows already carry their own insets, matching the padding=0 measured directly on the dropdown-menu component's nested panelSurface/content/menu node chain). `sm`/`md`/`lg` were insufficient for this real consumer, so the enum grew rather than having Dropdown Menu reach for `unstyled` and re-declare background/border/radius/shadow itself.

figmaSource.note: A single component (not a variant set) showing 8 repeated breadcrumb-item instances - no size/tone axis to capture.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 8-item demo renders every crumb - including the last - as an identical Link instance with no distinct 'current page' treatment. The component deliberately renders the last item in `items` as non-interactive text with aria-current="page" instead, per the WAI-ARIA Breadcrumb Pattern - documented here as an intentional adaptation, not a literal 1:1 reproduction.
Whether an item is 'current' is derived from the absence of `href`, not a separate isCurrent flag - simplest possible rule, consistent with Link's own required `href`.
iconBefore/iconAfter are exposed as arbitrary ReactNode, matching the BOOLEAN toggle properties Figma exposes on the breadcrumb-item part.

The current-page item no longer uses --color-content-default to visually distinguish it from ancestor links - per explicit design feedback, that differentiation wasn't wanted; it now uses the same --color-content-subtle as Link's own appearance=subtle, so every item in the trail reads at the same visual weight.

Link's own :visited treatment (a real browser-history-driven purple color swap) is intentionally overridden back to Link's normal resting/press color for every breadcrumb ancestor - per explicit design feedback, 'have you visited this URL before' isn't a signal breadcrumbs should surface, since it makes the trail read as a list of arbitrary hyperlinks rather than a location path. This is a documented, deliberate exception to the 'do not restyle Link's own hover/focus/press treatment' compositionRule below - it targets :visited specifically, not those states.

onCancel.description: Called when the cancel button (or Escape) discards the draft and reverts to value.

figmaLayoutData.actionButtonGroup: size=sm, shape=square, tone=default icon-buttons, cancel/close first then confirm/check, confirmed via screenshot of the state=edit variant

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 'state' axis (default/edit) is not implemented as a state or isEditing prop at all - editing state and the in-progress draft are owned entirely inside the component. Two earlier passes exposed isEditing externally (first fully controlled by the parent, then still controlled but toggleable); both were reverted after explicit design feedback that no real use case shows the confirm/cancel buttons before the field has been interacted with - editing must always start on click/focus.

state=default renders nothing but an empty slot - no read-only text, no pencil/edit icon, confirmed via screenshot. Rather than invent a separate read-mode display, Inline Edit clones the SAME single children element for both states via React.cloneElement (readOnly+value when not editing, draft+onChange when editing) - the same DOM node persists across the transition, so focus is never lost when editing starts on focus.

value/onConfirm mirror TextField's own controlled value pattern: the parent supplies the last confirmed value and receives it back via onConfirm only on commit, not per keystroke. Cancel discards the draft and reverts to value, calling onCancel with no value argument (the parent already has it).

Enter-to-confirm and Escape-to-cancel are an explicit addition beyond the two visible icon buttons Figma shows, confirmed as wanted by the user. Enter also calls preventDefault so a nested control inside a native <form> doesn't trigger an accidental submission. Both keys blur the field afterward (deselecting it), matching what clicking either action button already does - the same mousedown-set ref flag the action buttons use suppresses handleBlur's auto-confirm from re-firing off this same-tick blur.

children is expected to be a single controlled input-like element (TextField today, typically appearance=subtle so it reads as plain text at rest) rather than two separate read/edit elements the parent swaps between.

Figma's literal state=edit layout puts the action buttons trailing in the same row as the field, which would force the field to shrink to make room once editing starts. Per explicit design feedback, this implementation stacks the action row below the field instead (flex-direction: column, 8px gap, action row align-self: flex-end to anchor to the trailing/right edge) so the field keeps its full width in both states.

A consumer can raise siblingCount to get a wider range closer to Figma's sample.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma instances freely override width, height, and corner radius per usage rather than exposing them as named variants - the component formalizes the corner-radius axis as a `shape` prop (`rectangle` | `circle`, following Icon Tile's shape-prop convention) and leaves width/height to forwarded `style`/`className`, matching ProgressBar's existing convention for per-usage sizing.

Figma's prototype has an AFTER_TIMEOUT reaction smart-animating between the `default` and `subtle` variants every 1.5s as a way to preview a pulse effect inside Figma - the component instead implements the pulse as a self-contained CSS opacity animation on a single variant, so it animates on its own regardless of which `appearance` is selected.

sizingDetail.override: Forwarded style/className on the root div - no dedicated width/height props.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: A wrapping flex row (gap: spacing-sm) - the only styling Tag Group owns.

anatomy.name: visible tags
anatomy.description: tags.slice(0, maxVisible) (or every tag, when maxVisible is omitted), each a real Tag with every one of its own props forwarded, size applied uniformly.

anatomy.name: overflow tag
anatomy.description: Present only when tags.length > maxVisible. A Tag with isInteractive (Tag's plain-button form) reading overflowLabel(hiddenTags.length), wrapped in a DropdownMenu.

anatomy.name: overflow panel
anatomy.description: Dropdown Menu's Menu, one section (id: 'overflow') with one MenuItem per truncated tag - label, a decorative leadingElement from that tag's own elemBefore, and disabled mirroring that tag's own isDisabled.

tags.description: Every tag, visible and truncated. Each item is Tag's own props (minus size/children/isInteractive) plus a required id and a label (forwarded to Tag as children).

maxVisible.description: Once tags.length exceeds this, only the first maxVisible tags render - the rest are truncated behind the overflow tag. No truncation, and no overflow tag, when omitted.

size.description: Applied uniformly to every rendered tag, including the overflow tag.

alignment.description: Where the overflow tag renders relative to the visible tags - trailing (left) or leading (right). Does not change which tags are visible or truncated.

overflowLabel.description: The overflow tag's text, given the truncated count.

overflowMenuAriaLabel.description: Accessible name for the overflow panel (forwarded to Dropdown Menu's aria-label, then to Menu's role="menu" container).

onOverflowTagSelect.description: Called when a truncated tag is selected from the overflow panel. Tag Group does not navigate, remove, or close the panel on its own.

id.description: Applied to the root row element.

className.description: Composes with the root row element's class list.

tokens.note: tag-group.module.css declares exactly one token reference - gap: var(--spacing-sm), matching Figma's measured 8px itemSpacing/counterAxisSpacing on both axes of the wrap layout. Every other value is Tag's own tone/size tokens or Dropdown Menu/Menu's own panel/row tokens - see their respective contract.json files.

accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the overflow tag by Popup (via Dropdown Menu), reflecting the panel's open state
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the overflow tag by Popup, pointing at the panel id while open
accessibility.overflowPanelRole: menu (set by Menu, via Dropdown Menu), named by overflowMenuAriaLabel
accessibility.visibleTagAccessibility: unchanged from Tag's own documented accessibility - Tag Group applies no ARIA of its own to visible tags

figmaSource.note: The real Figma component set is named tab-group, not tag-group - a naming typo, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin. It is filed on the file's own "✅ Tag Group" page, and both variants are unambiguously a wrapping row of `tag` instances plus an eleventh `tag` (reading "+5 more") nested inside a `dropdown-menu` instance's trigger slot - not tabs. Code follows the real, verified structure under the correct name, TagGroup.
figmaSource.structure: Two variants cross a single `alignment` axis (left/right, default left). Each variant is an auto-layout frame (layoutWrap: WRAP, itemSpacing: 8, counterAxisSpacing: 8, counterAxisAlignItems: CENTER) containing ten `tag` instances (size=sm, tone=standard/default, isRemovable=false, elemBefore=false, text "Tag") plus one `dropdown-menu` instance (trigger=tag, alignment=left, isOpen=false) whose trigger slot holds an eleventh `tag` instance reading "+5 more" (same variant shape as the others: size=sm, tone=standard, isRemovable=false). In `alignment=left`, the dropdown-menu instance is the last child (trailing); in `alignment=right`, it is the first child (leading). The nested dropdown-menu's own `alignment` property measures `left` in both cases - it does not flip with the outer variant.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's example is a fixed illustrative count (10 visible tags + a "+5 more" overflow tag = 15 total, with no exposed count/list-editing property). Code generalizes this into an open, data-driven `tags: TagGroupItem[]` array plus a `maxVisible` number, the same 'closed demo becomes an open prop' adaptation Menu made for its own `sections` versus Figma's per-variant row instances.

Figma's `alignment` variant (left/right) became TagGroupProps.alignment directly, unchanged in name or values - it controls only where the overflow tag renders (trailing vs. leading), not which tags are visible or truncated, matching the fact that both Figma variants show the identical placeholder tag set.

The nested dropdown-menu's own `alignment` property was measured as `left` in both outer `alignment` variants (not flipped for `alignment=right`) - code matches this directly: TagGroup always renders the overflow tag's DropdownMenu with Dropdown Menu's own default alignment (left), rather than deriving or flipping it from TagGroup's own `alignment` prop.

The overflow tag's trigger needed a plain, focusable, non-navigational, non-removable interactive form - a gap in Tag's own code API (Tag was previously focusable only via `href` or its remove button). Added `isInteractive` to Tag itself (see tag.contract.json's own apiAdaptationNotes) rather than reimplementing a one-off interactive wrapper inside Tag Group.

Figma's nested `dropdown-menu` instance has an empty `content` slot in the static file (isOpen=false, never toggled open in the source), so the overflow panel's actual content (a Menu row per truncated tag) is a code-level design decision, not something measured from an open Figma variant - informed directly by Dropdown Menu's own established 'always renders a Menu built from sections' rule.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Bordered frame holding the optional before/action slots and the input; reacts to :hover and :focus-within.

anatomy.name: iconBefore
anatomy.description: Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative - never interactive.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.description: The real native text input; carries all forwarded native attributes.

anatomy.name: iconAfter
anatomy.description: Optional trailing icon or interactive action (e.g. an IconButton clear button). Never forced aria-hidden.

size.description: Frame height, padding, gap, and typography.

appearance.description: default is bordered at rest, rounded on all four corners; subtle has no visible border/background until hover, focus, or invalid, and always has square bottom corners.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and the error border (thicker, regardless of focus).

iconBefore.description: Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative (aria-hidden).

iconAfter.description: Optional trailing icon or interactive control (typically an IconButton clear action, or a Button). Never forced aria-hidden.

className.description: Composes with the root frame's class list.

inputClassName.description: Composes with the native input's class list.

requirements: Render a real native <input> - never fake one.
Set aria-invalid on the input when invalid is true.
iconBefore is aria-hidden - decorative only, never interactive.
iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden - it may hold a real interactive control (e.g. an IconButton clear action) which must keep its own accessible name and stay keyboard-reachable.
Text Field does not manage labelling - pair with a native label[htmlFor] or aria-label/aria-labelledby.

showCaret.note: Figma mockup-only, not a real prop.

placeholder.note: Figma mockup-only toggle between placeholder/value text, not a real prop.

elemBeforeInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the leading slot. Never interactive. The text case (e.g. a '$' currency prefix) is bound to fixed body-lg typography at every field size.

elemAfterInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the trailing slot. Frequently interactive (e.g. a clear action) - confirmed from a screenshot of the clear icon-button in its hover state. The icon-button case uses appearance=subtle, shape=square. A third `label` type was added later, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle) for compact metadata/status after the input (e.g. a unit or status pill) - confirmed directly from the component's own nested instance properties, not assumed. iconAfter is already typed React.ReactNode and .action is a plain centered flex wrapper, so a Label already renders correctly there with no component code changes.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 'state' axis (default/hover/focus/typing/filled) is not a real prop - verified from bound tokens: hover=:hover, focus=focus+empty (:focus-within + :placeholder-shown), typing=focus+has-value (:focus-within, not :placeholder-shown), filled=unfocused+has-value (not :placeholder-shown). All four derive from native pseudo-classes plus the input's own value; none are exposed as a prop.

Figma's 'tone' axis (standard/subtle) is renamed to 'appearance' (default/subtle) - a pure visual-weight distinction, matching this system's existing appearance vocabulary (see Button) rather than the semantic-meaning 'tone' word.
isInvalid renders with strokeWeight=2 even when not focused, confirmed directly from node data - invalid's thicker border is not a focus-only effect.

Figma's literal focus treatment thickens the frame's own border 1px->2px and swaps its color to --color-border-focus. Focus/typing replaces the resting border's color directly - the same pattern invalid already uses - rather than adding an outline ring around it, per explicit design feedback. Border width does not literally change to 2px, though: an earlier pass changed the real border-width on appearance=default's focus AND invalid, matching Figma directly, but that shifts the content box (and the placeholder/value text and typing caret) on every side, reported directly against the component from a side-by-side screenshot - both now paint the extra pixel via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px <color> instead, keeping border-width a constant 1px in the box model with zero layout impact.

Hover is suppressed once the field is focus/typing (:focus-within, or the pinned data-force-state='focus' reference) - hover should only ever be visible on an inactive field, per explicit design feedback.

showCaret and placeholder (BOOLEAN) component properties exist only to drive Figma's own mockup and have no code equivalent - a real input shows its own caret and switches placeholder/value automatically.

appearance=subtle's bottom corners are always square (border-bottom-{left,right}-radius: 0), confirmed directly from Figma's per-corner radius data on the subtle variants - only the top corners share appearance=default's radius.

appearance=subtle rests at the same 1px bottom border-width appearance=default uses at rest, per explicit design feedback (an earlier pass reserved a constant 2px transparent border specifically to avoid a layout shift; that reservation was reverted). Reverting it reintroduced the shift a real border-width change causes (the vertically-centered text visibly nudges by a pixel), so focus/invalid on appearance=subtle now paint the thicker look via box-shadow (inset 0 -1px 0 0 <color>) instead, keeping border-bottom-width a constant 1px in the box model at every state - zero layout impact. appearance.default's own invalid/focus still uses a real border-width change (a whole-box change on all four sides is a much smaller relative shift there), so this technique is specific to appearance=subtle.

`.root[data-invalid='true']` sets the border-width shorthand (all four sides) to 2px; `.appearance_subtle[data-invalid='true']` overrides border-top/right/left-width back to 0 and must also explicitly reset border-bottom-width back to 1px, or that side silently inherits the shorthand's leftover 2px and reintroduces the same text shift.

Hovering an invalid appearance=subtle field keeps the error border color rather than resetting to --color-border-input, per explicit design feedback - the border-color-changing hover rule is scoped with :not([data-invalid='true']); the background-changing hover rule is not, since hover should still tint the background on an invalid field.

elemBeforeInput and elemAfterInput are separate, asymmetric Figma components (icon|text vs icon-button|button), not a symmetric before/after pair - iconBefore is always aria-hidden, iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden.
Inline padding is asymmetric per size (tighter on the end side) and the icon/input gap varies per size (4px/6px/8px) rather than a flat 6px, confirmed directly from Figma's per-side bound variables.

elemAfterInput gained a third `type` option in Figma - `label` - alongside `icon` and `button`, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle, size sm/md). Since `iconAfter` is already `React.ReactNode` and `.action` is a plain centered flex wrapper, this required no component code change - only documenting the newly-supported content type.

anatomy.name: trigger
anatomy.description: The single child element (children) - any focusable control. Cloned by the underlying Popup to receive a measurement ref and aria-expanded/aria-controls.

anatomy.name: panel
anatomy.description: Popup's own default visual skin (background/border/radius/shadow), rendered with padding="none".

anatomy.name: menu
anatomy.description: A Menu, rendered with every DropdownMenu prop besides children/open/onOpenChange/alignment/id/className forwarded to it unchanged.

onOpenChange.description: Called with false on Escape or an outside click.

alignment.description: Maps to Popup's bottomLeft/bottomCenter/bottomRight - always opens below the trigger.

id.description: Applied to Popup's floating panel, not to Menu's root.

className.description: Composes with Popup's panel class list, not with Menu's root.

sections.description: Forwarded to Menu unchanged - see menu.contract.json.

tokens.note: DropdownMenu introduces no tokens of its own - every visible value comes from Popup (background/border/radius/shadow) and Menu (row/section/selection colors, spacing, typography, per-size width). See popup.contract.json and menu.contract.json.

triggeredBy: consumer-controlled - same as Popup, Dropdown Menu attaches no open/close handler itself
accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the trigger by Popup, reflecting open
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the trigger by Popup, pointing at the panel id while open
accessibility.role: menu (set by the inner Menu, not by DropdownMenu/Popup directly)
accessibility.focusManagement: left to the consumer, same as Popup and Menu - neither moves focus into the panel on open

figmaSource.structure: Variants cross `trigger` (avatar/icon-button/button/link-button/chip-base/chip-operator/chip-value/tag/page-selector - 9 distinct trigger types, default avatar) x `alignment` (left/center/right, default left) x `isOpen` (true/false, not fully crossed with alignment). Every variant instantiates the same `popup` component (the exact component set Popup wraps) with a `trigger` SLOT holding the trigger instance, and a `surface` SLOT holding `figma-parts / panelSurface` (Popup's own skin) whose own `content` SLOT holds a `menu` instance. The measured padding around that nested menu instance is 0 on every axis.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's 9-value `trigger` variant became a generic `children: React.ReactElement` prop, not a variant enum - matching Popup's own `children` model ("the single trigger element") rather than hardcoding a closed set of trigger shapes. Any focusable element works; the 9 Figma values are demonstrated in Storybook's Content story as examples, not enforced as an allowed list.

Figma's `alignment` (left/center/right) maps to Popup's `bottomLeft`/`bottomCenter`/`bottomRight` specifically - Dropdown Menu always opens below its trigger, matching the fact that Figma's dropdown-menu has no top/bottom axis at all. Popup's own viewport-fit fallback (trying the top* counterpart, then the remaining alignments) still applies underneath when there's no room below - a capability Figma doesn't model, inherited for free rather than re-derived.
`isOpen` became the existing `open`/`onOpenChange` controlled pair (Popup's own prop names), not a new prop - same native-attribute-first reasoning as Popup's own isOpen->open adaptation.

The measured zero padding around the nested `menu` instance is what motivated adding a fourth value, `'none'`, to Popup's own `padding` prop (see popup.contract.json apiAdaptationNotes, dated 2026-08-19) rather than having Dropdown Menu set `unstyled` and re-declare background/border/radius/shadow itself.

DropdownMenuProps extends MenuProps (minus id/className, which apply to Popup's panel instead) rather than accepting an opaque `content: React.ReactNode` the way Popup does - every real Figma instance of dropdown-menu nests a `menu` instance specifically, never arbitrary content, so the code API guides toward that same shape directly instead of requiring the consumer to manually construct a <Menu> every time.

anatomy.name: search
anatomy.description: Optional TextField (size="md", appearance="subtle", no leading icon) with a trailing clear button once there's a value, shown above sections when showSearch is true (default).

anatomy.name: section
anatomy.description: One per entry in `sections` - a leading divider, an optional heading row, and its list of items.

anatomy.name: divider
anatomy.description: Renders above every section, matching Figma's per-section leading separator - except the very first section when showSearch is false, since a divider there would float at the top edge with nothing above it to divide from.

anatomy.name: heading
anatomy.description: Optional section label with an optional leading icon.

anatomy.name: item
anatomy.description: One per entry in a section's `items` - a native button row with optional leading/title-leading/trailing slots, a label, and an optional description.

anatomy.name: loading-row
anatomy.description: Replaces the sections area entirely when `loading` is true - a Spinner plus loadingLabel.

anatomy.name: empty-message
anatomy.description: Shown in place of sections when search filters out every item.

size.description: Panel width only (192/240/288px) - row height always follows content.

showSearch.description: Matches Figma's own declared default. When true, the search field is autoFocused on mount - since Popup only mounts Menu while a Dropdown Menu is open, this focuses the search field every time the containing menu opens, with no extra wiring needed.

onSearchChange.description: Called on every search field change.

searchPlaceholder.description: Also used as the search field's aria-label when set.

showScrollbar.description: Matches Figma's own declared default. Maps to native overflow, not a custom scrollbar widget.

maxHeight.description: Caps the sections area's height before it scrolls.

loading.description: Replaces sections with a loading row.

emptyMessage.description: Shown when search filters out every item.

color.iconSelected: IconColor "selected" (--color-content-selected) - verified on a PLAIN elemBefore icon (not just checkbox/radio), which binds to the same color/content/selected variable id as the row's own text when isSelected=true; applies to any leadingElement icon whenever the row is selected, not just checkbox/radio-style rows.
color.iconUnselected: IconColor "default" (--color-content-default) for a plain unselected action row's icon; IconColor "subtle" (--color-content-subtle) specifically for the checkbox-empty/radio-unchecked glyphs, which are their own distinct low-emphasis indicator - both verified directly on their respective vector fills.

spacing.titleRowGap: --spacing-sm (gap between titleLeadingElement and label, inside the title row)

tokens.note: Selected-row background reuses existing semantic tokens (Figma's isSelected fills #e5f6ff/#ccecff/#b3e3ff resolved exactly to color-background-brand-primary-subtle-default/-hover/-press, already the brand.prussian.solid.100/200/300 aliases). Selected-row TEXT AND ICON color is a new semantic token, `--color-content-selected` (packages/ui/src/tokens/src/semantic/semantic-color-light.json and -dark.json) - it happens to equal `--color-content-brand-primary-default`'s value in both themes (prussian-900 light / prussian-500 dark), but Figma binds the title/description text to a genuinely distinct variable, `color/content/selected` (different variable id, own light/dark mode values, confirmed via figma.variables.getVariableByIdAsync - not the same variable as content/brand/primary/default, just a currently-identical one), so code mirrors that real distinction rather than collapsing it. Also added: IconColor `selected` on the shared Icon primitive (same category of addition as `discovery`, added for Inline Message). `--component-menu-width-*` is the only NEW dimension token (packages/ui/src/tokens/src/component/menu.json) - 192/240/288px don't land on the semantic spacing scale (max --spacing-4xl is 40px), matching Tooltip's precedent of a dedicated component-tier dimension token for an off-scale Figma value.

keyboardInteraction: ArrowDown/ArrowUp move a roving tabIndex (and DOM focus) between enabled, visible items, wrapping at either end.
Home/End jump to the first/last enabled, visible item.
Enter/Space activate the focused item for free - it's a real <button>.
A disabled item is excluded entirely from the roving-tabindex cycle.
requirements: Every rendered item is a real <button role="menuitem" | "menuitemcheckbox" | "menuitemradio">, so Enter/Space activation and :disabled semantics are native, not simulated.
aria-checked is set only when selectionType is provided - plain action rows with just `selected` never get a stray aria-checked.
Only one item at a time carries tabIndex={0}; every other item is tabIndex={-1} (roving-tabindex pattern) - the container itself carries tabIndex={-1} as a non-tab-reachable fallback focus target.

leadingElement/trailingElement/titleLeadingElement/headingLeadingElement are always rendered with aria-hidden="true" - the row's own accessible name comes from its text content, never from these slots.

figmaSource.structure: Variants cross `menus` (1/2/3 - number of sections shown in the design canvas) with `size` (sm/md/lg - panel width only, 192/240/288px; row height is unaffected). Two boolean component properties, `showSearch` and `showScrollbar`, both default true. Each section is a `code-parts / <section>/list` instance with its own leading `separator` (a divider) and a `Slot` filled by `code-parts / <menu-item>` instances - code renders that leading divider above every section except the very first when showSearch is false, a design-review correction (a divider with nothing above it to divide from otherwise). The section's own Container padding is asymmetric - spacing/xs (4px) top, spacing/sm (8px) bottom, not a uniform padding-block - confirmed directly against a live-edited Figma instance. The root `menu` component has empty `fills`/`strokes` - no background/border/shadow of its own.

subComponentsVerified.name: menu-item
subComponentsVerified.note: state (default/hover/press/focus) x isSelected (false/true) x isDisabled (false/true), 9 of 16 combinations modeled. Component properties: descriptionText, showDescription, showElemBefore, showElemAfter, optionText, showTitleElemBefore.

subComponentsVerified.name: menu-search
subComponentsVerified.note: A `text-field` instance, `size="md"` and `tone="subtle"` - mapped to code as a composed TextField with `size="md"` `appearance="subtle"` (TextField's own prop names for the same concepts), not a bespoke input. Direct inspection of the actual instance (not just its component-property defaults) confirmed `elemAfterInput` (the clear icon-button) is used, but no leading `elemBeforeInput` icon - the search field has no leading icon at all. The outer `code-parts / <menu-search>` wrapper itself only has default/focus/typing variants - no hover variant at all - and the nested text-field instance's own `fills`/`strokes` are empty ([]) in every one of those three states. Code therefore neutralizes TextField's own `appearance="subtle"` hover-background and focus-underline rules specifically inside Menu's `.search` wrapper (a local-class-plus-global-attribute-selector override, no `!important`) rather than relying on `appearance="subtle"` alone, which still shows both. That override needs `[data-size='md']` plus two `:not()` clauses to reach sufficient specificity - TextField's own hover rule stacks three `:not()` clauses of its own (specificity (0,5,0)), higher than a bare `:hover` override (0,3,0) would reach.

subComponentsVerified.name: heading-item
subComponentsVerified.note: elemBefore slot + {title} text - mapped to code as `section.headingLeadingElement` + `section.heading`.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma models menu-item content as free-floating slots inside a component-set variant grid (state x isSelected x isDisabled), not a data structure. Code inverts this into a `sections: MenuSection[]` prop - each item a plain object (`MenuItem`) - so a real list of N items doesn't require N manually-composed component instances.

leadingElement/trailingElement are typed as arbitrary React.ReactNode but are documented as decorative-only in code: a real interactive Checkbox/Radio/Button nested inside the row's own <button> would be invalid HTML. This matches Figma exactly, not just a code-side precaution - the file's own 'checkboxes'/'radios' slot-content demos (menu-item Parts group) swap elemBefore's nested icon INSTANCE_SWAP property to the icon components `checkbox_fill`/`checkbox-empty`/`radio_checked`/`radio_unchecked` (colored `color/content/brand/primary/default` when checked, `color/content/subtle` when not - i.e. IconColor `brand`/`subtle`), never to a real Checkbox/Radio component. Selection semantics are carried by the row's own `selected`/`selectionType`, not by whatever's rendered in the slot. Every elemBefore icon (including plain, non-selectable action rows) uses the icon wrapper's `Size: md` + `spacing: spacious (24px)` component properties - code maps this to Icon's `spacing="spacious"` (size="md" is already Icon's own default).

selectionType ('checkbox' | 'radio') is a code-level addition with no direct Figma component property - inferred from the same 'checkboxes'/'radios' slot-content demos above, which show real-world compositions where isSelected pairs with a checkbox/radio-shaped row. Modeled per-item rather than as a menu-level 'selectionMode' so a single menu can mix plain action rows with a selectable group.

isSelected=true adds a 2px left indicator with `strokeAlign: INSIDE` and `paddingLeft` left completely unchanged (still spacing/md, identical to every other row) - code maps this to an inset box-shadow (`--border-width-md` `--color-border-brand-primary`) rather than `border-left`, since a real border-left would add to the row's box size in CSS and shift selected-row content 2px right relative to unselected rows, which Figma's own inside-aligned stroke does not do.

showScrollbar's Figma value renders a custom decorative scrollbar-thumb graphic (a `<scrollbar-thumb>` instance, visible in the menus=2/3 variants once a `scrolling container` wraps the sections). Code maps this to native `overflow-y: auto`/`hidden` instead of reproducing the custom thumb widget - a deliberate simplification, not a design-parity gap that's expected to close later.

Arrow-key roving-tabindex navigation (ArrowUp/Down/Home/End) has no Figma variant at all - it's a code-level accessibility decision for the ARIA menu pattern, delivering on Popup's own contract.json futureEnhancements note ('a documented recipe for wiring keyboard arrow navigation once Dropdown Menu exists').
